revision_notes: ITU DataHub (2024) records LTE/WiMAX population coverage at 87%, below the 90% implied by the single original source (a non-authoritative aggregator). Downgraded to Value Code 4 (75-89%).

Definition: Percentage of individuals who used the internet (from any location, via any device) in the last three months. This measures actual internet adoption beyond network availability, capturing the combined effect of infrastructure, affordability, digital literacy, and relevance.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed: World Bank WDI records 57.62% individuals using the internet (2023) and DataReportal cites 57.6% (2025), corroborating the original figure. Value Code 4 (50-69%) confirmed.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source conflates SIM/connections penetration (139% of population per GSMA/DataReportal; 133% per ESCCOM) with 'unique mobile subscribers', a distinct metric this variable requires. No authoritative unique-subscriber percentage for Eswatini was located in GSMA Intelligence or ITU data. Downgraded to Value Code 0 (Unknown) and flagged for human review rather than guessed.

Definition: Percentage of mobile connections using smartphones (as opposed to feature phones or basic phones). Smartphones are the minimum device requirement for accessing most digital public infrastructure services, apps, and mobile internet.

revision_notes: Original source (94% 'broadband connections') measured the wrong metric. Definition: The availability and presence of major cloud service providers (hyperscale and regional) operating in or serving the country with local or near-local infrastructure. Cloud availability determines access to scalable computing resources for government, business, and startups.
Value Name: Served remotely from distant regions only (>100ms latency)
Comments: Regional access, local push via Google [[Techpoint](https://techpoint.africa/news/eswatini-partners-with-google-to-drive-digital-transformation-and-economic-growth/)]
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: AWS (af-south-1, Cape Town), Azure (South Africa North/West) and Google Cloud (africa-south1, Johannesburg) all operate availability zones in the same SADC sub-region, with measured terrestrial latency of only 6-10ms from Johannesburg to Eswatini, well below the >100ms implied by the original score. Upgraded to Value Code 3 (regional availability zone nearby).

Definition: The country's overall cybersecurity preparedness, based on the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index (GCI). Covers legal measures, technical measures, organisational measures, capacity development, and cooperation. Essential for trust in stored data and digital services.

revision_notes: ITU GCI 2024 score for Eswatini is 79.43, which falls in the 60-79 'Advancing' band (Value Code 4), not the 80+ 'Role-modelling' band (Value Code 5) originally assigned. The figure itself was correctly sourced but miscoded against the scale; corrected to Value Code 4.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Legislation enacted with Data Protection Authority established
Comments: Data Protection Act enacted with Commission [[DataProtection Africa](https://dataprotection.africa/eswatini-data-protection-act-introduced/)]

revision_notes: Confirmed via the Data Protection Act, 2022 (Act No. 5 of 2022) and ESCCOM's designation as national Data Protection Authority under s.5. Value Code 4 (legislation enacted with DPA established) confirmed with primary legal text.

Definition: Percentage of national population with access to electricity (grid or off-grid). This is the primary indicator of energy infrastructure availability for ICT. Based on World Bank/IEA Tracking SDG7 data, national statistical offices, or Afrobarometer surveys.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: World Bank WDI records 86.4% access (2023); a 2025 World Bank project document puts the current rate at approximately 88%, still below the 90% threshold used for the original score. Downgraded to Value Code 4 (75-89%), consistent with the figure already in the Comments field.

Definition: Frequency and severity of power outages experienced by businesses and households. Based on World Bank Enterprise Surveys, Afrobarometer, or national utility data. Reflects the quality of electricity supply beyond mere access — critical for running ICT equipment and data infrastructure.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The 2024 World Bank Enterprise Survey country profile confirms 58.5% of Eswatini firms experience electrical outages, and the cited c.1.2 outages/month implies roughly 14 per year — above the '<10 per year' threshold for Value Code 4. Revised down to Value Code 3 (moderate, monthly outages), from the same source.

Definition: Percentage of total electricity generation from renewable sources (hydro, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). Indicates energy sustainability and potential for distributed power solutions relevant to ICT infrastructure in off-grid areas.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: World Bank/IEA data (EG.ELC.RNEW.ZS) places Eswatini's renewable electricity output at approximately 83% of total generation, and IRENA-sourced generation data (via countryeconomy.com) show renewable generation at 97% (2024); both are far above the single original source's 36%, which appears to understate domestic hydro/bagasse generation. Revised up to Value Code 5 (75%+); note Eswatini also imports significant thermal power from South Africa, not counted in domestic generation statistics, so the picture for consumption would differ.

Definition: The gap between urban and rural electricity access rates. A smaller gap indicates more equitable energy distribution, critical for ensuring ICT infrastructure can serve the whole population, not just cities.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: World Bank SE4ALL data (2020) show urban access at 92.2% and rural at 75.8%, a gap of 16.4 percentage points — this matches the figure already in the Comments field but is inconsistent with the Value Code of 5 (Gap <10pp) that was assigned. Corrected to Value Code 4 (Gap 10-20pp); more recent narrative World Bank and CIA Factbook estimates suggest the gap may have since narrowed, so this indicator merits periodic re-check.
